about: Which side of the left-right scale each real party label in the game's data sits on: -1 the Democratic family, +1 the Republican family, 0 any other party, independents and nonpartisan labels. A label is matched exactly (case and spacing aside), never by a pattern in code. A fusion label (two parties nominating one candidate) takes the side of the major party in it. A state's affiliate of a national party takes the national party's side. Puerto Rico's parties are organized on status, not on the national parties; each takes the side its leadership and most of its officeholders affiliate with nationally. A label not listed is 0.
source: Party labels as printed in the Clerk of the House's 2024 election statistics (data/source/electoral-calibration-2024) and the Open States rosters (data/research/offices/legislature-party-counts-2026.json); affiliations from the Democratic National Committee and Republican National Committee state party lists (democrats.org/who-we-are/state-parties, gop.com/leadership/state-parties) and, for New York's and Connecticut's fusion lines, N.Y. Elec. Law § 7-104 and Conn. Gen. Stat. § 9-453t.

congressCaucus.about: The side a label caucuses with in Congress where it isn't the label's own: both independent U.S. senators of the 119th Congress (Angus King, Bernie Sanders) caucus with the Democrats.

notes.Partido Nuevo Progresista: Statehood party; its governor and resident commissioner since 2021 (Jenniffer González-Colón) caucus as Republicans. Some of its members are Democrats; the party as a whole takes the Republican side.
notes.Partido Popular Democrático: Commonwealth party; its national figures affiliate with the Democratic Party.
notes.Partido Independentista Puertorriqueño: Independence party; affiliated with neither national party: side 0.
notes.Independent Republican: Not the Republican Party's line: side 0.
